title: Fundamentals
chapter_outcomes: Using software tools for the creation and editing of digital graphics, including: graphics tools, including: add layers, remove layers, select active layer, order, toggle visibility, lock/unlock layers, change opacity/transparency, blend/flatten/merge layers; transform tools, including: resize, skew, reflect, rotate, move, scale, shear, apply envelope and perspective; grouping or merging tools, including: group, ungroup, combine/join, add/subtract, intersect; alignment and distribution tools, including: left, right, top, bottom, centre alignment, vertical and horizontal distribution, order, raise, lower, bring to front, send to back; layout tools, including: rulers, grids, guidelines, snapping; colour picker tools, including select a colour or colour range within an image or from other sources; crop tools, including crop/clip to objects; colour systems, including: RGB, HSL, CMYK, CMS, how each produces colour, their properties, purpose and uses; the need for different image resolutions, including the impact of having too low/high resolution for an image on screen or in print; different bitmap and vector file formats, including their suitability and selection for use in a given scenario; exporting an image in different file formats, including: SVG, BMP, JPG/JPEG, PNG, GIF, TIF, PDF; changing solid and gradient fills

Using software tools for the creation and editing of vector graphics, including: creating a vector graphic that meets the requirements of its intended application and audience; vector drawing tools: freehand drawing, Bezier curves, straight lines, shape tools – creation of rectangles, ellipses, circles, arcs, stars, polygons and spirals, application of envelopes and perspectives; selection tools to select and manipulate parts of a vector graphic, including: convert to curves, replication, transformation tools; fill tools to colour elements, including: solid, gradient; node and path editing, including: adding, moving and deleting nodes to simplify paths, using Bezier handles, working with symmetrical, asymmetrical, cusp, and smooth nodes, align and distribute nodes
Converting bitmap images into editable vector shapes, including trace bitmaps
Advantages and disadvantages of converting a bitmap image into an editable vector shape

Using software tools for the creation and editing of bitmap graphics, including: creating and editing bitmap images that meet the requirements of their intended application and audience; selection tools to select, remove or hide parts of a bitmap image, including: lasso, magic wand, colour select, cut-out, crop, masking tools; working with colour, including: solid and gradient fills, convert to black and white, greyscale, adjust brightness, contrast, colour balance, shadows and highlights; brush, pencil and pen tools, including: pre-set and customised options; tools/filters to alter parts of an image, including: distort, clone, erase, blur, smudge, sharpen, red eye removal; resizing the image/canvas, including the use of: changing colour depth, changing resolution
Methods of compression: lossless compression, lossy compression
Effects of different methods of compression on images
Selecting font style, including: font face, size, kerning, letter spacing, line spacing
Fitting text to path or shape: aligning text along a line or around a shape
Converting text to curves: converting fonts into editable vector shapes
Use of text and its manipulation within graphics software
